title: Psalms Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 26.

questions.question: In Psalms 26, who is the author of this Psalm?
questions.explanation: The Psalm is introduced as 'A Psalm of David' in Psalms 26:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 26:1, why does the Psalmist say he shall not slide?
options: Because he has walked in integrity
Because he has trusted in the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because he has trusted in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:1 states, 'I have trusted also in the LORD; therefore I shall not slide.'

questions.question: What does the Psalmist ask the LORD to do in Psalms 26:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:2 says, 'Examine me, O LORD, and prove me; try my reins and my heart.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 26:2 asks the LORD to try the Psalmist's reins and heart.
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states, 'try my reins and my heart.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 26:3, what is before the Psalmist's eyes?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:3 says, 'For thy lovingkindness is before mine eyes.'

questions.question: What has the Psalmist walked in, according to Psalms 26:3?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I have walked in thy truth.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 26:4 says the Psalmist has sat with vain persons.
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:4 states, 'I have not sat with vain persons,' meaning he avoided them.

questions.question: Who does the Psalmist say he will not go in with, according to Psalms 26:4?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'neither will I go in with dissemblers.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 26:5, what has the Psalmist hated?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:5 states, 'I have hated the congregation of evil doers.'

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 26:5, the Psalmist says he will sit with the wicked.
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'and will not sit with the wicked.'

questions.question: What symbolic act does the Psalmist say he will do in Psalms 26:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:6 states, 'I will wash mine hands in innocency.'

questions.question: Where does the Psalmist say he will compass, according to Psalms 26:6?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'so will I compass thine altar, O LORD.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of washing hands and compassing the altar in Psalms 26:7?
options: To publish thanksgiving and tell of God’s wondrous works
To seek mercy from the king
questions.correctAnswer: To publish thanksgiving and tell of God’s wondrous works
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:7 says, 'That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works.'

questions.question: In Psalms 26, which comes first: the Psalmist asking to be judged or the Psalmist stating he has not sat with vain persons?
options: Stating he has not sat with vain persons
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:1 starts with 'Judge me, O LORD,' and Psalms 26:4 mentions not sitting with vain persons, so asking to be judged comes first.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 26:3 indicates that the Psalmist has walked in God's truth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:3 explicitly states, 'and I have walked in thy truth.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 26:5, how does the Psalmist describe his attitude toward the congregation of evil doers?
options: He loves them and seeks to join them
He hates them and refuses to sit with the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: He hates them and refuses to sit with the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:5 clearly states that the Psalmist 'hated the congregation of evil doers; and will not sit with the wicked,' showing his rejection of evil company and desire to remain separate.

questions.question: What symbolic action does the Psalmist take in Psalms 26:6 to express his innocence and devotion?
options: He washes his hands in innocency and surrounds the LORD's altar
questions.correctAnswer: He washes his hands in innocency and surrounds the LORD's altar
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:6 states, 'I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O LORD,' indicating a ritual cleansing symbolizing purity as he approaches God's altar.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 26:7, what is the Psalmist’s purpose for approaching the LORD’s altar with clean hands?
options: To publish thanksgiving and tell of God's wondrous works
questions.correctAnswer: To publish thanksgiving and tell of God's wondrous works
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 26:7, the Psalmist approaches God's altar to 'publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works,' emphasizing praise and testimony.

questions.question: How does Psalms 26:8 express the Psalmist’s feelings about the place of God's presence?
options: He fears the habitation of God's house
He loves the habitation of God's house and the place of His honor
He avoids the place where God’s honor dwells
He questions the value of God's house
questions.correctAnswer: He loves the habitation of God's house and the place of His honor
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:8 states, 'LORD, I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth,' showing deep affection and reverence for God's dwelling.

questions.question: What does Psalms 26:9 request concerning the Psalmist’s association with sinners and bloodthirsty men?
options: Gather not his soul with sinners, nor his life with bloody men
questions.correctAnswer: Gather not his soul with sinners, nor his life with bloody men
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:9 asks the LORD, 'Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men,' requesting separation from evil and violent people.

questions.question: What characterizes the hands of the men described in Psalms 26:10?
options: Their hands are clean and pure
Their right hands are full of bribes and they work mischief
Their hands are empty and powerless
Their hands are used to bless others
questions.correctAnswer: Their right hands are full of bribes and they work mischief
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:10 describes these men as having 'mischief' in their hands and their right hand full of bribes, indicating corruption and wrongdoing.

questions.question: How does the Psalmist describe his own conduct in Psalms 26:11?
options: He walks in integrity and asks for redemption and mercy
He boasts of his righteousness without humility
He remains silent about his ways
questions.correctAnswer: He walks in integrity and asks for redemption and mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:11 says, 'But as for me, I will walk in mine integrity: redeem me, and be merciful unto me,' showing a commitment to righteousness and a request for God's mercy.

questions.question: What does Psalms 26:12 say about the Psalmist’s position and his response in the congregation?
options: His foot stumbles and he curses the LORD
His foot stands in an even place and he blesses the LORD in the congregation
His foot is unstable and he hides from the congregation
His foot is swift to flee from the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: His foot stands in an even place and he blesses the LORD in the congregation
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:12 declares, 'My foot standeth in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the LORD,' showing stability and public praise.

questions.question: What does Psalms 26:6 promise will happen if one washes their hands in innocency and surrounds the LORD's altar, according to the adjacent verse?
options: They will publish thanksgiving and tell of God’s wondrous works
They will be ignored by God
questions.correctAnswer: They will publish thanksgiving and tell of God’s wondrous works
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:6 speaks of washing hands in innocence and compassing God's altar, and Psalms 26:7 immediately follows that this leads to publishing thanksgiving and telling of God's wondrous works, linking ritual purity to joyful praise.

questions.question: According to Psalms 26:8, what is the significance of loving the habitation of God's house in relation to the Psalmist's integrity in Psalms 26:11?
options: Loving God's house contradicts walking in integrity
Loving God's house supports the Psalmist's walk in integrity and plea for mercy
Loving God's house leads to isolation
Loving God's house is unrelated to integrity
questions.correctAnswer: Loving God's house supports the Psalmist's walk in integrity and plea for mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:8 shows love for God's dwelling place, which complements Psalms 26:11 where the Psalmist commits to integrity and asks for redemption, showing a holistic devotion to God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 26:5 teach us about choosing our company in relation to Christian living?
options: It encourages us to mingle freely with all people
It teaches to avoid sitting with evil doers and wicked to maintain integrity
It suggests ignoring the behavior of others
It advises joining sinners to influence them
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches to avoid sitting with evil doers and wicked to maintain integrity
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:5 states the Psalmist hates evil doers and refuses to sit with the wicked, emphasizing the importance of separating from corrupt company to live righteously.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 26:7 indicates that the Psalmist's thanksgiving is silent and private.
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:7 says the Psalmist will 'publish with the voice of thanksgiving,' indicating that his thanksgiving is vocal and public rather than silent and private.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 26:9 requests the LORD to gather the Psalmist’s soul with sinners and bloody men.
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:9 explicitly asks the LORD, 'Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men,' showing a desire to be kept separate from evil, not gathered with them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 26:12 shows the Psalmist’s confidence in standing firm and blessing the LORD publicly.
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:12 states, 'My foot standeth in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the LORD,' indicating confidence and public praise.

questions.question: If a believer wants to avoid being associated with wickedness, what practical truth from Psalms 26:5 and 26:9 applies?
options: They should engage actively with sinners to reform them
They should hate evil doers and ask God not to gather their soul with sinners
They should ignore the presence of evil around them
They should accept all people regardless of behavior
questions.correctAnswer: They should hate evil doers and ask God not to gather their soul with sinners
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:5 expresses hatred toward evil doers and refusal to sit with the wicked, while Psalms 26:9 requests God not to gather the Psalmist with sinners, teaching believers to separate themselves from wickedness.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 26.

questions.question: According to Psalms 26:9, what does David ask the LORD not to do with his soul?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:9 explicitly says, 'Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men,' indicating David's plea to be kept apart from sinners.

questions.question: In Psalms 26:10, what is said to be in the hands of the wicked?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'In whose hands is mischief, and their right hand is full of bribes,' showing the wicked's actions are characterized by wrongdoing.

questions.question: What does David declare he will do in Psalms 26:11 despite the wickedness around him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:11 says, 'But as for me, I will walk in mine integrity,' highlighting David's commitment to righteousness.

questions.question: Which phrase from Psalms 26:12 reflects a theme of stability and worship?
options: My foot standeth in an even place
I have trusted in the LORD
I will wash mine hands in innocency
questions.correctAnswer: My foot standeth in an even place
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states, 'My foot standeth in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the LORD,' symbolizing stability and public worship.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'redeem me, and be merciful unto me' in Psalms 26:11 in relation to the Old Testament concept of redemption?
options: It echoes the concept of God as a redeemer who saves from sin and judgment.
It refers to a financial transaction for freedom.
It is a plea for military rescue from enemies.
It signifies the redemption of land possessions.
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the concept of God as a redeemer who saves from sin and judgment.
questions.explanation: David's plea in Psalms 26:11 aligns with the Old Testament theological theme of God as redeemer, as seen in passages like Isaiah 44:22 where God redeems from sin.

questions.question: What literary device is found in the structure of Psalms 26:6-7 where washing hands in innocence is followed by praising God's wondrous works?
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 show synonymous parallelism, linking ritual purity ('wash mine hands') with the resulting praise ('publish with the voice of thanksgiving'), a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of refusing to associate with the wicked as expressed in Psalms 26:5?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 4:14-15 warns against entering the path of the wicked, paralleling David's declaration in Psalms 26:5 of hating the congregation of evil doers.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 26:8, David expresses a deep affection for the temple as the dwelling place of God's honor.
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:8 states, 'LORD, I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth,' showing David's love for the temple.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 26:2 asks the LORD to ignore the condition of the psalmist’s heart and reins.
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:2 calls on the LORD to 'examine me... try my reins and my heart,' so the statement is false because it asks for careful examination, not ignorance.

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'mischief' in Psalms 26:10 carries the connotation of 'evil plan' or 'calamity'?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ra' (רַע) is often translated as 'evil' or 'mischief' and is used in Psalms 26:10 to describe the wicked's hands full of wrongdoing.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of walking in integrity and purity as David expresses in Psalms 26:11?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 8:21 states, 'Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men,' echoing the integrity theme in Psalms 26:11.

questions.question: How does the phrase 'My foot standeth in an even place' in Psalms 26:12 metaphorically relate to the concept of righteousness in biblical literature?
options: It symbolizes stability and uprightness in moral conduct.
It indicates the need for pilgrimage.
It describes a physical location in the temple.
It refers to a legal judgment.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes stability and uprightness in moral conduct.
questions.explanation: Standing with one's foot in an even place metaphorically conveys moral steadiness and righteousness, consistent with biblical imagery of right standing before God (Psalms 26:12).

questions.question: In Psalms 26:4, why does David say he will not sit with dissemblers, and what does this reveal about his character?
options: Because he values sincerity and integrity
Because he wants to avoid poverty
questions.correctAnswer: Because he values sincerity and integrity
questions.explanation: David's refusal to sit with dissemblers (hypocrites) in Psalms 26:4 reflects his commitment to honesty and moral purity.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book also uses the theme of 'washing hands in innocence' as a symbol of purity, similar to Psalms 26:6?
questions.explanation: Job 9:30 uses 'I wash my hands in innocence' to symbolize purity, paralleling Psalm 26:6's use of the imagery for ritual and moral cleanliness.

questions.question: What historical or cultural context helps explain David's concern about 'bribes' in Psalms 26:10?
options: Corruption was common in ancient Near Eastern legal systems.
It was a metaphor for harvest offerings.
Bribes were considered a form of worship.
questions.correctAnswer: Corruption was common in ancient Near Eastern legal systems.
questions.explanation: Bribery in ancient Near Eastern courts was a known problem, leading to injustice, which David condemns in Psalms 26:10.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David claim as the basis for his confidence that he will not 'slide' according to Psalms 26:1?
options: He has walked in integrity and trusted the LORD
He has abundant wealth and power
He has many allies among the people
questions.correctAnswer: He has walked in integrity and trusted the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 26:1 states David's confidence is rooted in his integrity and trust in the LORD, which prevents him from slipping.

questions.question: In Psalms 26:2, what two inward parts does David ask God to examine and prove?
questions.explanation: David requests God to examine and test his reins (kidneys, representing the inner person) and heart, highlighting personal holiness (Psalms 26:2).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Psalms 26:3, where lovingkindness is described as before the psalmist's eyes?
questions.explanation: The lovingkindness (steadfast love) of God is explicitly mentioned as being before David’s eyes, showing God's enduring, covenantal love (Psalms 26:3).

questions.question: According to Psalms 26:4, with whom does David refuse to associate?
questions.explanation: David explicitly states he has not sat with vain persons nor will he join with dissemblers, indicating separation from deceitful and worthless company (Psalms 26:4).

questions.question: What doctrine regarding separation from evil is taught by combining Psalms 26:5 and Psalms 26:10?
options: Believers must hate evil and avoid those who practice mischief and bribery
Believers should tolerate sinners to bring them to repentance
Evil is not to be feared but embraced for growth
Righteous people should seek to join sinners for influence
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must hate evil and avoid those who practice mischief and bribery
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 10 together teach that the believer must hate the congregation of evildoers and avoid those whose hands are full of mischief and bribes, affirming the doctrine of sanctified separation from wickedness (Psalms 26:5, 26:10).

questions.question: What symbolic act does David perform in Psalms 26:6 that signifies his innocence and approach to God's presence?
questions.explanation: David declares he will wash his hands in innocence, symbolizing purity before approaching and encircling God's altar (Psalms 26:6).

questions.question: What is the main purpose of David's approach to God's altar as described in Psalms 26:7?
options: To publish thanksgiving and declare God's wondrous works
questions.correctAnswer: To publish thanksgiving and declare God's wondrous works
questions.explanation: David intends to give thanks aloud and proclaim all the marvelous works of the LORD, showing the purpose of worship is praise and testimony (Psalms 26:7).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 26:8 by David's love for the habitation of God's house?
questions.explanation: David’s love for the habitation of God’s house and the place where His honor dwells signifies reverence for God's holy presence (Psalms 26:8).

questions.question: How does Psalms 26:9 reflect a doctrine of divine separation in the life of the believer?
options: David asks God not to gather him with sinners or violent men
David requests to be united with all men regardless of sin
David seeks to convert sinners by close fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: David asks God not to gather him with sinners or violent men
questions.explanation: David prays that his soul not be gathered with sinners or violent men, expressing a desire for God’s protective separation from wickedness (Psalms 26:9).

questions.question: What does David affirm about his conduct in Psalms 26:11, and what is his plea to God?
options: He will walk in integrity and asks for redemption and mercy
He confesses sin and asks for punishment
He boasts of his strength and demands victory
He remains silent and waits for judgment
questions.correctAnswer: He will walk in integrity and asks for redemption and mercy
questions.explanation: David commits to integrity in his walk and petitions God for redemption and mercy, highlighting the need for divine grace alongside personal righteousness (Psalms 26:11).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about sanctification and stability is taught by combining Psalms 26:1 and Psalms 26:12?
options: Integrity and trust in God provide a firm, stable footing and cause one to bless God publicly
Material success guarantees spiritual stability and public praise
Human effort alone secures a stable spiritual life
Isolation from the community is necessary for holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity and trust in God provide a firm, stable footing and cause one to bless God publicly
questions.explanation: Verse 1 emphasizes walking in integrity and trusting God to not slide, while verse 12 states the foot stands in an even place and blesses the LORD in the congregation, teaching sanctification brings stability and public worship (Psalms 26:1, 26:12).

questions.question: How does Psalms 26:6-7 together demonstrate the relationship between personal holiness and worship?
options: Personal innocence prepares one to proclaim thanksgiving and God's works
Worship is independent of personal purity
Only ritual sacrifices matter in worship
Personal holiness is irrelevant to public praise
questions.correctAnswer: Personal innocence prepares one to proclaim thanksgiving and God's works
questions.explanation: David’s washing hands in innocence (v6) enables him to approach God's altar and publish thanksgiving and declare God's works (v7), linking holiness with authentic worship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 26 teaches self-righteousness rather than true repentance. What does Psalms 26:2-3, 11 actually teach about the believer's heart posture?
options: Believers invite God’s examination and seek mercy despite walking in integrity
Believers rely solely on their own works for salvation
Believers reject God's judgment as unfair
Believers claim perfection without need for mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Believers invite God’s examination and seek mercy despite walking in integrity
questions.explanation: David asks God to examine his inner being (v2), acknowledges God’s lovingkindness (v3), and pleads for redemption and mercy (v11), showing humility and dependence, not self-righteousness.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection to the broader redemptive story is illustrated by David’s refusal in Psalms 26:4-5 to associate with evildoers?
options: The call to holiness and separation from sin as a pilgrim people
The promise of earthly political dominion
The triumph of Israel’s military power
questions.correctAnswer: The call to holiness and separation from sin as a pilgrim people
questions.explanation: David’s hatred of the congregation of evildoers (v5) and avoidance of vain and deceitful persons (v4) reflects Israel’s calling to be holy and separate, a theme central to the covenant narrative (Psalms 26:4-5).

questions.question: Which doctrine about divine justice and human corruption is revealed in Psalms 26:10?
options: Unrighteous hands and bribery characterize the wicked
Bribery is acceptable in certain contexts
questions.correctAnswer: Unrighteous hands and bribery characterize the wicked
questions.explanation: The verse describes sinners as having mischief in their hands and their right hand full of bribes, illustrating the doctrine of human corruption and divine justice against such practices (Psalms 26:10).
